html:
The Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks are huge geometric enclosures of earth built in southern Ohio by the Hopewell culture between about 1 and 400 CE. In 2023 eight of them became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Walls of earth form perfect circles, squares and octagons, some covering many hectares. The Octagon at Newark is aligned to the 18.6 year cycle of the moon's risings and settings, showing careful astronomy without writing.

The sites were places of ceremony and burial, not towns. Goods found there came from far away: copper from Lake Superior, obsidian from the Rockies and shells from the Gulf of Mexico, signs of a wide exchange network. Centuries later the Mississippian people built Monks Mound at Cahokia, after the earlier mounds of Poverty Point.
